chapter: Chords, recordings and his own groups
title: How he learned to read: Mel Bay and classical piano books
summary: He learned counting from a Mel Bay beginner book then classical piano books until he could read fairly well.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I want to ask you more about the system of your guitar playing.

The system that I had, a lot of people don't wanna accept it. See, it was a long time before I even knew what I was doing myself. I knew that I was playing but I didn't know anything --- no music. But then I just took it up and got me
a book and started to add + one + one and two + two, 'cause there's a lot of counting in music and the notes would be going by in a hurry.

I think it was a Mel Bay book. First grade, kindergarten. To learn how to spell. Notes one and two... like I said that 'and' is mean... After that a while I started with piano classical books. The notes were outstanding and I could pick out out of the whole book... maybe 3 times I could play, get by with. Gradually, like that till I could go so I could read fairly good. Not a whole lot 'cause I still did never go to any school or nothin. Then playing 4 strings is awkward 'cause you run out of strings. Then you got to take up, just like a train switchin tracks...
